question: Our GitHub Actions job on ubuntu-latest runs every spec in headless Firefox, and we set `autoRecord: false` in the config to keep runs quick. All our `record` steps come back SKIPPED. The docs say the `browser` engine records without a display, so I added `"engine": "browser"` to each record step, but they're still SKIPPED. How do I get these Firefox recordings?

facts.text: The `browser` engine records only Chrome (a Chrome tab), so a Firefox `record` step with `engine: "browser"` is SKIPPED.

Headless Firefox can't be recorded, so its `record` steps are SKIPPED; to record it, run Firefox headed (`headless: false`) with the `ffmpeg` engine and install Xvfb on the Linux runner, or switch the context to Chrome, which records headless.

With `autoRecord` on (the default), Doc Detective runs headless Firefox headed when the host can capture the screen (such as with Xvfb installed), so its `record` steps record; setting `autoRecord: false` keeps Firefox headless.

must_not: Headless Firefox can be recorded with no display or Xvfb, through some engine, flag, or config option.

wrong.why: headless set on the context, not the browser
says the browser engine records Firefox
wrong.answer: The `browser` engine records Firefox and Chrome alike, but only when the browser is headed. Keep `"engine": "browser"` and set `headless: false` on Firefox; the engine captures the Firefox tab without a display, so you don't need Xvfb.

replace.from: Your `autoRecord: false` matters here. While `autoRecord` is on, which is the default, Doc Detective runs headless Firefox headed when the host can capture the screen, and its `record` steps then record too. With it off, Firefox stays headless.
